## Overview

Add retry-observable external Elastic EP operations and bounded native submission.
The native coordinator owns resize execution; an HTTP caller need not remain
connected through preparation, draining, joining, and collective commit.

Follow-up to #43202 and related to #42515 and
[Dynamo DEP #13121](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13121).

## Claims

- Preserve synchronous `/scale_elastic_ep`, optional operation/runtime IDs,
  retained latest-operation replay, and atomic effective-topology evidence.
- Add `/submit_elastic_ep`: validate and retain an immutable request, acknowledge
  local participation promptly, and observe its native-owned execution through
  the existing status endpoint. Caller disconnect does not cancel that execution.
- Bind each local receipt to operation, instance, base-topology token, absolute
  target, drain timeout, and owned range. Refuse conflicting replay, unresolved
  supersession, stale instances, and delayed new requests after a successor.
- Keep correlated status/replay reachable while inference admission is closed,
  including on a retired API process. Retired owners refuse new work before
  replacing their successful retirement receipt. Acceptance is not collective completion
  and completion is not a current inference-health signal.

## Validation

Qualified independently on published head `9ea2c30931f0892c18561cb933ca48ffcb218136`
on 2026-10-27, using four B200 GPUs and BF16 DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat
(model revision `85864749cd611b4353ce1decdb286193298f64c7`).

- Normal native protocol suite: **34 passed** (11 unrelated cases deselected).
- Native real-serving GPU suite: **2 passed**: synchronous EP2 → EP3 and bounded
  EP2 → EP3 → EP2. Assertions cover a deliberately dropped acknowledgment,
  identical replay, conflicting payloads, terminal local receipts, delayed stale
  requests, and refusal of new work on a retired owner without losing its
  successful retirement replay.
- Tests use this standalone PR's Python source and the official CUDA 13 native
  wheel for its compiled-source-compatible upstream base `b4a0830f6`; no bootstrap,
  local-range, or unpublished composition patches were added.
- All applicable pre-commit checks pass, including mypy, Ruff, Markdown, SPDX,
  CI test tethering, and configuration checks. Feature-scoped whitespace checks pass.
- The native test cleanup emitted descendant/resource-tracker warnings; allocated
  GPU memory returned to its pre-test level. This run does not establish
  fault-tolerant recovery, model-quality parity, or performance.
- GitHub-source documentation discovery passes. The rendered PR preview has not
  been verified for this head.

Reproduction in a supported native environment:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py \
  -k 'external_elastic_ep or validate_expert_capacity_on_every_rank' -q
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 TP_SIZE=1 DP_SIZE=2 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py \
  -k test_external_lb_elastic_ep_scale_up -vv -s
```

## Details

Reuse the existing coordinator, epoch-scoped TCPStore and native resize path.
The API process owns one tracked execution task and one latest immutable local
receipt, not an additional transaction framework. A new request uses the current
instance and opaque topology token; replay uses its original immutable body.
Observe delivery/completion per existing client as well as collective topology.
No receipt is expired by wall-clock timeout. Runtime restart changes the instance
and invalidates old authority.

Ray and ordinary synchronous launches keep their existing APIs. Automatic
bootstrap (#62973) and native local-range resizing
([follow-up](https://github.com/julienmancuso/vllm/pull/1)) remain separate. Packed
composition requires the local-range delegation to forward operation identity;
this standalone PR does not import their bootstrap/process ownership changes.

Duplicate checks found no other bounded external submission proposal; #62973
supplies launch discovery, not this operation contract. AI assistance was used
for code, tests, documentation, and checks. The human submitter remains responsible
for reviewing the complete diff and native qualification.

 - `/scale_elastic_ep` - Trigger scaling operations
 - `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` - Check if scaling is in progress
 
+### External scaling operation status
+
+With external DP load balancing, `POST /scale_elastic_ep` accepts optional
+`operation_id` and `expected_instance_id` fields:
+
+```json
+{
+  "new_data_parallel_size": 4,
+  "drain_timeout": 120,
+  "operation_id": "resize-42",
+  "expected_instance_id": "<instance_id from this rank's status>"
+}
+```
+
+Send the same operation ID and target to every existing rank, using each rank's
+own instance ID. The orchestrator still launches joiners and controls routing.
+`POST /is_scaling_elastic_ep` reports the latest operation's ID, epoch, phase,
+requested and effective DP sizes, topology certainty, and error.
+
+Replaying the latest operation with the same target returns its active or terminal
+status without repeating the resize. A conflicting target or operation, or a stale
+instance precondition, returns HTTP 409. A target already equal to the current DP
+size remains a no-op; status describes the last actual resize. This API retains
+only the latest operation, so controllers must finish reconciling it before
+starting another.
+
+When `topology_known` is false, the effective size is the last known size.
+Further operations are rejected; replaying the failed operation remains available
+for observation. Restart the runtime before issuing another resize. Inference
+admission remains closed after commit failure, while health and status remain
+queryable. These fields do not provide an engine recovery mechanism.
+
+### Bounded external scaling submission
+
+Use `POST /submit_elastic_ep` when your orchestrator must return before joining
+engines start or a collective finishes. This opt-in route requires externally
+managed Elastic EP; synchronous `/scale_elastic_ep` and Ray callers keep their
+existing behavior.
+
+Read `POST /is_scaling_elastic_ep` on each existing client and retain its
+`instance_id` and opaque `topology_token`. Send the same operation and target to
+every existing client, with that client's original instance and token:
+
+```json
+{
+  "operation_id": "resize-42",
+  "expected_instance_id": "<this client's instance_id>",
+  "base_topology_token": "<this client's topology_token>",
+  "new_data_parallel_size": 4,
+  "drain_timeout": 120
+}
+```
+
+HTTP 202 acknowledges only this client's participation, not delivery to its
+peers or completed membership. Native execution continues independently of the
+HTTP connection. Status exposes the retained `local_submission`, including the
+owned `first_rank`/`local_size`, execution progress and error. Observe collective
+completion and every client's finished receipt, then check inference readiness.
+Serving readiness remains engine/runtime-owned, not an orchestrator grant.
+
+After a timeout or lost response, replay the identical body with its original
+instance and token. A terminal replay returns HTTP 200; conflicting reuse or a
+stale new request returns HTTP 409. One client's refusal does not establish that
+the collective was rejected. Pending or uncertain participation cannot be
+superseded. The latest receipt remains observable for the API process lifetime
+until a safe successor is accepted; tokens change on acceptance and commit, so
+delayed old requests cannot start again after that successor. A process restart
+changes its instance and requires external recovery.
+
+A retired client rejects new operations without replacing its retained retirement
+receipt. Status and identical replay of that retirement remain available.
+
 ## Process Checkpoint APIs
 
 For external checkpoint/restore orchestrators, available with `--enable-sleep-mode`. Preparing drains the engine and releases its KV cache and other external state, any number of times. Until `/checkpoint/restore`, new requests get a retryable error and `/health` still returns 200, as while asleep. `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` prepares each engine once it starts.

Thanks, fixed in [a004a3e](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a004a3e801948dc7469700eb02e3bad2215144a2) in bootstrap polling rather than mutating `active_epoch` during terminal replay, since that field also routes worker notifications.
